mainTopic: The order of the משנה, and how 'אהא' and 'אהא נאה' work as נזירות vows
overview: This amud first finishes a discussion about the order of the משנה. The משנה opened with כינויים (substitute words for נזירות) but explained ידות (partial phrases) first. The גמרא explains that ידות come from a דרשה, so they are dear to the תנא. It adds that a תנא opens with the main subject but explains his favorite topic first. Then the גמרא turns to the case of 'אהא' ('I will be'). שמואל says it counts when a נזיר was passing by and the speaker meant נזירות in his heart, even though his words alone were not fully clear. Next comes 'אהא נאה' ('I will be beautiful'), which could mean beautifying מצוות. שמואל answers that the speaker was holding his hair. The amud ends by asking how נזירות, a matter linked to sin, can be called 'beautiful', and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: The inheritance משנה also had its own reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge from the משנה of יש נוחלין. That משנה explains its first-listed category first, but it does so for its own reason: it puts the main inheritance case first.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the משנה of 'יש נוחלין' as well, the תנא explains the main case of inheritance first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is answering a challenge to the rule that a תנא explains the last thing he listed first. The משנה of יש נוחלין seemed to break that rule by explaining its first category first, and the גמרא says it had a special reason for its order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה of יש נוחלין explains its first-listed category first, which seems to go against the rule. The גמרא answers that the תנא had a reason there: he wanted to explain the main, basic inheritance case first. So that משנה is an exception with its own reason, not a disproof of the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Some inherit': the opening words of a משנה in בבא בתרא about inheritance
The main, basic case of inheritance

phrases.english: Regarding 'There are those who inherit' as well,
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in בבא בתרא that the גמרא brought up earlier as a challenge, since it explains its first category first.

phrases.english: he explains the main case of inheritance first.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues answering, from before this section, the counterexamples raised against the rule that a תנא explains the last-listed item first.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects using the משנה of יש נוחלין as a counterexample to the rule that the last-listed item is explained first.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That משנה had its own reason: it puts the main inheritance case first.

steps.title: Then here the משנה should explain כינויים first
steps.stepSummary: The original question comes back: since a תנא does explain the main item first when he has a reason, why doesn't our משנה explain the כינויים first?
steps.simpleTranslation: But then here, let him explain the substitute words first!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its first question. Just as the תנא in those משניות explained the main case first, our משנה should explain the כינויים first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 showed that a תנא sometimes explains the first, main item first when he has a reason. Here the משנה listed כינויים first, so it should explain them first too. Yet it starts with ידות ('אהא'), so the question is open again. The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: Substitute words, like changed forms of the word 'נזיר' that still mean a vow

phrases.english: But then here, let him explain the substitute words first!
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording. 'Here' means our משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 1 shows that a תנא sometimes explains the main item first, the original question about the order of our משנה is back.
steps.kashyaTarget: The order of explanation in our משנה (ידות explained before כינויים).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Like the משניות that explain their main item first, our משנה should explain the כינויים, which it listed first, before the ידות.

steps.title: ידות are dear to the תנא because they come from a דרשה
steps.stepSummary: The real reason is given: ידות are learned from a דרשה, so the תנא loves them and explains them first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is the reason: since ידות come to him from a דרשה, they are dear to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new answer for why ידות are explained first. The תנא treasures them because they are learned through a דרשה of the פסוקים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ידות are not written openly in the Torah. They are learned by carefully working out the פסוקים. Something learned through that effort is precious to the תנא, so he explains it first.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Handles': partial phrases that show a person means a vow
A teaching worked out from the פסוקים

phrases.english: Rather, this is the reason:
ידות, since they come to him
from a דרשה, are dear to him.

steps.terutzResolutionType: New reason that replaces the earlier rejected explanation
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the order should follow the list, so כינויים should be explained first.
steps.terutzMaskana: ידות are explained first because the תנא treasures what comes from a דרשה.
steps.whatToRemember: ידות are explained first because they are learned from a דרשה, and that makes them dear to the תנא.

steps.title: Then the משנה should open with ידות too
steps.stepSummary: If ידות are so dear, the משנה should have opened with them, not with כינויים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let him open with them at the very beginning!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes on the last answer. If the תנא loves ידות so much, why didn't he mention them first in the opening line of the משנה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in step 3 explains why ידות are explained first. But the same reason should make them come first in the opening list too. Yet the משנה opens with 'כל כינויי נזירות'.

phrases.english: Then let him open with them first!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 3 by applying it to the opening line.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer that ידות are dear to the תנא.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being dear puts ידות first in the explanation, it should also put them first in the opening line.

steps.title: Open with the main topic, explain the favorite first
steps.stepSummary: The תנא opens with the main subject of נזירות, but when he starts explaining, he begins with his favorite, ידות.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the תנא begins, he begins with the main subject. But when it comes to explanations, he explains ידות first.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the opening and the explanation follow different rules. The opening line goes to the main topic, and the explanation starts with what is dear.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two separate decisions here. The first line of a משנה names the main subject, which is the basic נזירות rule from the Torah. Once the explaining starts, the תנא is free to begin with ידות, which he loves.
steps.whatToRemember: The תנא opens with the main subject of נזירות, but he explains ידות first because they are dear to him.

phrases.english: When the תנא begins —
he begins with the main subject,
phrases.notes: Literally 'the main קרבן'. It points to the basic נזירות vow, which comes straight from the Torah.

phrases.english: but when it comes to explanations —
he explains the ידות first.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנָּא כִּי מַתְחִיל מַתְחִיל בְּעִיקַּר קׇרְבָּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 and closes the discussion about the order of the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the case: the opening and the explanation follow different rules
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Being dear should put ידות first everywhere, even in the opening line.
steps.terutzMaskana: The opening line names the main subject, and the explanation starts with ידות.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: saying 'אהא' makes one a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the first case of the משנה: someone who says 'אהא' ('I will be') is a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who says 'I will be' is a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic and quotes the first case in the משנה. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אהא' is a יד, an unfinished phrase. The person never actually said the word 'נזיר', yet the משנה says it still counts as a vow of נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: A person who takes the vow of נזירות

phrases.english: One who says 'I will be' is a נזיר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion about order ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying only 'אהא' is enough to make a person a נזיר.

steps.title: Maybe he meant 'I will be fasting'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: 'I will be' is unclear. Maybe he meant he would fast, not become a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps he is saying 'I will be fasting'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's ruling. 'I will be' could finish in many ways, such as 'I will be fasting'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A יד only works if it clearly points to the vow. 'אהא' by itself is open-ended. It could just as easily mean a vow to fast, so why should we assume נזירות?

phrases.english: Perhaps he is saying 'I will be fasting'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling of the משנה quoted in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ruling that 'אהא' makes one a נזיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'אהא' has more than one possible meaning, so it should not clearly count as a נזירות vow.

steps.title: שמואל: a נזיר was passing by
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה is talking about a case where a נזיר was passing in front of the speaker, so 'I will be' clearly means 'like him'.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: for example, when a נזיר was passing in front of him.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question by setting the case. A נזיר was walking by when the man said 'אהא', so it is clear he meant 'I will be a נזיר like him'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words alone are unclear, but the setting makes them clear. When a נזיר is right in front of him, 'I will be' points to נזירות and not to fasting.
steps.whatToRemember: 'אהא' works as a נזירות vow when the setting makes it clear, such as when a נזיר is passing by.
steps.confusionAlert: שמואל is not saying that 'אהא' always makes one a נזיר. It works because the passing נזיר shows what the man meant.

phrases.english: שמואל said:
For example, when a נזיר was passing in front of him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל כְּגוֹן שֶׁהָיָה נָזִיר עוֹבֵר לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7 by setting the משנה's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case: the משנה speaks about a specific setting
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אהא' might mean fasting, so it shouldn't count as נזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: A passing נזיר makes it clear that 'אהא' means 'I will be a נזיר'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This teaches that a יד can depend on the setting: unclear words can still form a vow when the situation shows what the person meant.

steps.title: Does שמואל hold that unclear partial phrases do not count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that שמואל needed a passing נזיר because he holds ידים שאינן מוכיחות לא הוויין ידים.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that שמואל holds that unclear partial expressions do not count as expressions?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks whether שמואל's answer shows that he takes a side in a known question: whether an unclear partial vow phrase still counts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל said 'אהא' works only when a נזיר is passing by. That could suggest that, without that clue, an unclear phrase is not binding. If so, שמואל would be taking a side on ידים שאינן מוכיחות.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (introduces a suggestion the גמרא may reject)
'handles': partial or shortened expressions of a vow
partial expressions that are not clear and do not prove what was meant

steps.confusionAlert: Here 'יָדַיִם' does not mean hands. It means partial phrases that 'hold onto' a full vow.

phrases.english: Shall we say that Shmuel holds
that partial expressions that are not clear
are not considered partial expressions?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a possible conclusion from שמואל's answer in step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's need to explain the case as one where a נזיר is passing by.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'אהא' needs the passing נזיר to work, it seems שמואל holds that unclear partial phrases are not binding.

steps.title: A passing נזיר makes the words clear; with no clue, they are truly ambiguous
steps.stepSummary: The suggestion is rejected. Without any נזיר present, 'אהא' could mean 'I will be fasting', so it is not even a partial phrase for נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: They say: when a נזיר is passing in front of him, there is no room to think he meant something else. But when no נזיר is passing, we say he may have meant 'I will be fasting.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that שמואל took a side. The plain word 'אהא' is simply too vague to mean anything on its own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question about ידים שאינן מוכיחות applies to phrases that point toward a vow but not clearly. A bare 'אהא' does not point toward נזירות at all, since it could just as easily mean fasting. So שמואל's ruling says nothing about that question.

phrases.english: They say:
When a nazir is passing in front of him,
there is no room to doubt that he means another matter.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל וַדַּאי אֵין הַנָּזִיר עוֹבֵר לְפָנָיו,
phrases.english: But when certainly no nazir is passing in front of him,
we say:
perhaps he is saying "I will be fasting."

steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that שמואל holds ידים שאינן מוכיחות are not binding.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A bare 'אהא' is not an unclear partial phrase for נזירות. It is fully ambiguous, since it could mean fasting.

steps.title: Maybe he only meant to pay for the נזיר's offerings
steps.stepSummary: Even with a נזיר passing, 'I will be' might mean 'I will be the one who covers his קרבנות.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he meant to free the נזיר from paying for his own offerings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's case again. A passing נזיר still does not prove that the speaker wants to become a נזיר himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר must bring קרבנות at the end of his נזירות. Saying 'I will be' while a נזיר passes by could mean 'I will take on his costs', not 'I will be a נזיר like him.'

keyTerms.meaning: to exempt him, to free him from an obligation

phrases.english: But perhaps he is saying it to exempt him
from his offerings?
phrases.notes: He means: I will pay for the animals this נזיר has to bring.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the clarity that step 10 gave to the passing-נזיר case.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's claim that a passing נזיר makes 'אהא' clearly mean נזירות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: There is another reasonable meaning connected to the passing נזיר: taking on his קרבנות.

steps.title: He had נזירות in mind
steps.stepSummary: The case is one where the speaker meant נזירות in his heart.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case is where he said it in his heart, meaning he intended to become a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is talking about someone who really intended נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His words could mean either thing, so his inner intention decides. Since he meant נזירות, he is a נזיר.

keyTerms.meaning: in his heart, in his mind

phrases.english: Where he said it in his heart.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא) to one where the person intended נזירות.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אהא' might mean paying for the נזיר's קרבנות.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה is speaking of someone whose heart intended נזירות.

steps.title: If he meant it, why does the משנה need to say it?
steps.stepSummary: If he intended נזירות, it seems obvious that he is a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what is the point of saying it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer. If the person meant נזירות, the ruling looks too obvious to need teaching.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A משנה is expected to teach something new. Once we know he intended נזירות, it seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: what is there to say? (it is obvious)

phrases.english: If so, what is there to say!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of step 12 as making the משנה obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation that he intended נזירות in his heart.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If his intention was clear, the ruling teaches nothing new.

steps.title: You might think mouth and heart must fully match
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that unclear words backed by real intention are enough, even though the words do not spell out the vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said that we need his mouth and heart to match exactly. So the משנה teaches us that this is enough.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what is new in the משנה: you might have thought the words must be as clear as the thought.
steps.deeperAnalysis: One could think a vow needs the spoken words to fully state what the heart means. The משנה teaches that words which can mean נזירות, together with real intention, are enough.
steps.whatToRemember: With a נזיר passing by and נזירות in his heart, 'אהא' makes him a נזיר, even though his words alone did not clearly say so.

phrases.english: You might have said:
we require his mouth and heart to be the same,
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא: בָּעִינַן פִּיו וְלִבּוֹ שָׁוִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 13 by showing what is new in the משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: shows what a learner might have wrongly thought.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A vow counts only if the spoken words fully match the inner intention.
steps.terutzMaskana: Words that can mean נזירות, together with real intention, are enough.

steps.title: Next case in the משנה: 'I will be beautiful'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: one who says 'אהא נאה' is a נזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'I will be beautiful' makes him a נזיר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה. It is setting up a new question about this phrase.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה treats 'beautiful' as a partial phrase for נזירות. The usual understanding is that a נזיר grows his hair, which is called his beauty. The גמרא will now ask whether that meaning is clear enough.

phrases.english: "I will be beautiful" — he is a nazir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the 'אהא' discussion and moves to the next phrase in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Saying 'אהא נאה' makes a person a נזיר.

steps.title: Maybe 'beautiful' means beautiful in מצוות
steps.stepSummary: 'I will be beautiful' could mean 'I will beautify myself before ה' with מצוות.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But perhaps he meant: I will be beautiful before Him with מצוות?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. 'Beautiful' may have nothing to do with נזירות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase has another religious meaning: doing מצוות in a beautiful way. If so, 'אהא נאה' should not clearly mean נזירות.

phrases.english: But perhaps he meant: I will be beautiful before Him with מצוות?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the ruling quoted in step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that 'אהא נאה' means נזירות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Beautiful' has a well-known other meaning: beautifying מצוות.

steps.title: A ברייתא shows that 'beautiful' can mean beautiful מצוות
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא on 'זה אלי ואנוהו' explains beauty before ה' as making beautiful מצוות.
steps.simpleTranslation: As a ברייתא teaches: 'This is my God and I will glorify Him' means I will be beautiful before Him in מצוות: a beautiful סוכה, לולב, and ציצית, and a beautiful ספר תורה wrapped in beautiful silk.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports its challenge with a ברייתא that uses 'beautiful' in exactly this מצוה sense.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This shows that the other meaning is a real, known way of speaking, so the challenge has weight. The next step answers it with שמואל's explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: as it was taught in a ברייתא
This is my God and I will glorify Him

steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא is the source for the idea of הידור מצוה, doing מצוות in a beautiful way.

phrases.english: As it was taught in a baraisa:
"This is my God and I will glorify Him"
phrases.notes: שמות 15:2. The word 'ואנוהו' shares a root with 'נאה'.

phrases.english: I will be beautiful before Him in מצוות.
I will make before Him a beautiful sukkah,
a beautiful lulav, beautiful tzitzis,
I will write before Him a beautiful Torah scroll
and wrap it in beautiful silk cloths!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the challenge of step 16 with a ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That 'נאה' can mean beautifying מצוות rather than נזירות.

steps.title: He was holding his hair when he spoke
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה's case is one where the speaker held his hair while saying 'I will be beautiful,' which shows he means נזירות.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל said: The case is where he is holding his hair and says, 'I will be beautiful.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 16. 'I will be beautiful' counts as a נזירות vow when the man says it while holding his hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words alone could mean beautifying oneself with מצוות. Holding his hair shows that the 'beauty' he means is his hair, and a נזיר grows his hair. His action removes the doubt and points the unclear words toward נזירות.

keyTerms.meaning: I will be beautiful (I will beautify myself)

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that an action done together with unclear words can make their meaning clear enough to create a נזירות vow.

phrases.english: Shmuel said:
[The case is] where he is holding his hair,
phrases.notes: Holding his hair shows he is talking about his hair, which a נזיר lets grow.

phrases.english: and he said, 'I will be beautiful.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from steps 16 and 17 that 'beautiful' could mean beautifying oneself with מצוות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case (אוקימתא): the speaker's action makes his meaning clear
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'I will be beautiful' could mean beautifying oneself before ה' with מצוות, so it should not create נזירות.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because he is holding his hair, his words clearly refer to growing his hair as a נזיר.

steps.title: Can נזירות, a matter of sin, be called beautiful?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how something called a 'matter of transgression' can be described as 'beautiful.'
steps.simpleTranslation: נזירות is a matter of sin, and we call it 'beautiful'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges שמואל's answer. If נזירות is linked to sin, it seems strange that the vow would use the word 'beautiful' for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמואל's answer assumes that 'I will be beautiful' means 'I will be a נזיר.' The גמרא points out that נזירות is viewed as connected to sin. So how can the vow describe it as something beautiful? This question sets up the answer that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: נזירות, the state of being a נזיר
A matter of transgression, something linked to sin

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a ruling that נזירות is forbidden. It is a question about wording: why would something linked to sin be called 'beautiful'?

phrases.english: Naziriteship is a matter of transgression,
and we call it 'beautiful'?

steps.triggerLanguage: נְזִירָא מִילְּתָא דַעֲבֵירָה וְאָמְרִינַן לֵיהּ נָאֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges שמואל's answer in step 18, which says 'beautiful' refers to the נזיר's hair.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's reading that 'I will be beautiful' means taking on נזירות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Something considered a matter of sin cannot properly be called 'beautiful,' so the word 'נאה' does not seem to fit נזירות.
